suggestions.assertion: D1 Diagram drawn / D2 Coverage and truth
suggestions.reason: Neither says whether one node that groups several tasks counts. This run merged three finished tasks into a single 'T1 to T3' node: a legitimate simplification, yet it hides T1->T2 and T1->T3 and which predecessor feeds T4 versus T5-T7. I passed D1 and failed D2, but another grader could go either way. State the rule ('each of T1...T11 has its own node or ID' or 'grouped done tasks are allowed if edges stay faithful'). D1 and D2 also overlap on coverage.

The assertion text (a heading or banner naming the audience) is met by 'Part A (for Dana)' and 'Part B (for the AI agent)', but check_doc.py's A1 check demands <!-- zone: --> markers, so the judged result (pass) and the mechanical result (Major) disagree. Decide whether audience-named H2s are enough or the markers are required.

The judged placement ('straight after the title and one metadata line') is not what the checker measures. It counts text lines before the first blockquote, table or image, and here a 'Convention' blockquote at L9 hid five header bullets (two of them reading and contents pointers) before the bottom line. A numeric limit would make this repeatable, for example a bottom line within N lines of the title with no contents or pointer lines before it.

suggestions.assertion: D5 D6 Explained and reproducible / E1 E2 Honesty
suggestions.reason: Both bundle several rules, so a run that satisfies most of them fails outright. D5/D6 here had alt text, legend, a .dot source and a text equivalent but no reading caption or relation statement. E1/E2 here had strong E2 (tags, unknowns table) and no E1 (no confidence levels). Splitting them would show which part the skill actually improves.

No assertion checks that the decision list equals the six open questions with extras labelled. This run re-labelled Q3-Q6 (all 'need a human decision' in open-questions.md) as 'unblock others' and added an unsourced Q7 with an invented date; C4 catches it only by interpretation, and Dana's view passes regardless. An explicit check such as 'decision list = open questions 1-6, additions marked as the author's proposal' would score this consistently.
It passes when the bullet says 'Q1 to Q4' and only the figure says 'T4 to T7'. Require the dependency and the 30 Oct threshold to be stated in the panel text itself if that is what is intended.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong discriminating checks (A3, B1, C2, C3, Agent-ready, Guardrails, F3), but several outcomes depend on interpretation (D1/D2 grouped nodes, C1 placement, A1 markers vs headings, C4 labelled additions) and two bundled assertions (D5 D6, E1 E2) hide partial success. Clarify those and add a check that the decision list matches the sources.
